summary: An excerpt from a novel (labeled Book 12, part 68) in which Lexy meets a naval officer on the road near Wyngate. He explains that he came back from sea for repairs, received Caroline's letters, and had met her on the steamer Ormond, where they bonded while her parents were seasick. Caroline's family disapproved of him because he has no money beyond his pay, and she agreed to meet him at Wyngate, the nearest main-line station to a place where her former nurse or governess, Miss Craigie, lived. The passage ends with Lexy moved to tears and the officer's account unfinished.
one_line: Lexy meets a naval officer near Wyngate who reveals his secret romance with Caroline, begun aboard the steamer Ormond.
key_facts: Lexy meets a naval officer who says he came back to port because the engines broke down after bad weather, and he went to repair the ship.
The officer obtained leave from the old man (his commanding officer) for some very important business and traveled to Wyngate.
Mrs. Royce told the officer that Lexy had gone out to the Queltons' house, which he did not like.
The officer met Caroline about a year earlier on board the Ormond, where she and her parents were seasick most of the time.
Caroline's letters were posted by a servant girl called Annie, and the officer wrote to Caroline in care of Annie's mother.
The officer says he has no money, only his pay, but that it was enough for the two of them to live on.
The officer says, "I'm not a beggar. I can hold my own pretty well in the world, and I could look after a wife."
The officer asked Caroline to marry him and told her he could not give her much but they could have had a jolly sort of life.
Caroline's family, the Enderbys, did not appreciate the officer, and Caroline told him that visiting her people was no use.
Caroline arranged to meet the officer in Wyngate because it is the nearest station of the main line to a place where a nurse or governess of hers lived.
Lexy says she is sorry for the officer and admits she is a little bit crying.
Lexy says "I know it!" with vehemence, feeling indignant against the Enderbys and anyone who did not appreciate him.
